original_question:
For the two-component complex vector version of the modified NLS model, where v is C^2-valued and satisfies

 i P_2(epsilon nabla) partial_tau v + (Delta_perp + alpha_1 partial_z^2)v + i alpha_2 v + (1/3)(1 + i epsilon alpha_3 . nabla)((v . v)v + 2|v|^2 v) = 0,

can one investigate the vectorial counterparts of the scalar open problems studied in the paper, including the analogues of the questions about global existence versus blow-up, pulse splitting, self-steepening, mixed effects, and long-time approximation of the underlying Maxwell equations?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 9 in §4.4: “Investigate the vectorial counterparts for (3)vect of the various open problems formulated for the scalar equation (3) in Sects. 4.1–4.3, and 4.5.”
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the target as the vectorial C^2-valued NLS-type model introduced as (3)vect, and it correctly understands that the paper asks for vectorial analogues of earlier scalar open problems rather than a brand-new unrelated problem. The examples you name—global existence versus blow-up, pulse splitting, self-steepening, mixed effects, and longer-time approximation of Maxwell—do match several of the scalar open problems that §4.4 is pointing back to, especially Open Problems 4–8 and 10. The displayed PDE is also essentially the right model, modulo the precise cubic vector nonlinearity.
missing_details: The exact target is Open Problem 9 in §4.4, not an informal umbrella question.
§4.4 fixes, 'for simplicity', the cubic case only, i.e. f = 0 in the scalar family (3). Your draft does not state that restriction.
The exact vectorial cubic term is the paper’s isotropic expression (1/3)(1 + i ε α3·∇)[(v·v) conj(v) + 2|v|^2 v]; your draft omits the conjugation on the final factor of the first summand.
The paper works with v : [0,T) × R^d -> C^2, with d and the interpretation of α1 tied to the GVD regime: α1 = 0 (no GVD), α1 = 1 (anomalous GVD), α1 = -1 (normal GVD).
The operator P2(ε∇) is not arbitrary: in §1.1 it is assumed to be a second-order-at-most, self-adjoint, positive operator.
The parameter assumptions from §1.1 are missing: ε > 0 is small, α2 >= 0, and α3 ∈ R^d.
The draft does not mention Remark 2, which is important context: the scalar equation (3) is recovered from (3)vect when the initial data lie in a one-dimensional real subspace of C^2.

The paper’s official formulation is broader than the subset you list: Open Problem 9 points back to all earlier scalar open problems in §§4.1–4.3 and 4.5, including Open Problems 1 and 2 (modified-nonlinearity oscillatory behavior and the ε -> 0 behavior past scalar blow-up), Open Problem 3 (ionization models), Open Problem 4 (partial off-axis well-posedness/global existence), Open Problem 5 (self-steepening blow-up scenarios), Open Problems 6 and 7 (global existence and pulse splitting in normal GVD), Open Problem 8 (mixed partial off-axis/self-steepening effects), and Open Problem 10 (longer-time Maxwell justification).
The time/frame convention is implicit in your draft: equations (3) and (3)vect are written in the frame moving with group velocity and with rescaled time (the paper uses τ = ε t in §1, then t in §4).

The long-time approximation issue is more specific than 'long-time approximation of Maxwell': §4.5 asks for a rigorous justification of one of the NLS-type models on a time interval [0, T/ε] with T >= T_foc.
refined_question:
For the cubic vectorial NLS-type model considered in §4.4, namely

i P2(ε∇)∂t v + (Δ⊥ + α1∂z^2)v + i α2 v + (1/3)(1 + i ε α3·∇)[(v·v) conj(v) + 2|v|^2 v] = 0,

with v : [0,T) × R^d -> C^2, ε > 0, P2(ε∇) a second-order-at-most self-adjoint positive operator, α1 ∈ {0, ±1}, α2 >= 0, α3 ∈ R^d, and with the scalar equation recovered when the initial data lie in a one-dimensional real subspace of C^2 as in Remark 2, can one investigate the vectorial counterparts of the scalar open problems posed earlier in the paper in §§4.1–4.3 and 4.5—namely the corresponding questions about modified-nonlinearity dynamics, global existence versus finite-time breakdown, pulse splitting, self-steepening, mixed partial-off-axis/self-steepening effects, and rigorous justification of the underlying Maxwell equations on time scales [0, T/ε] with T >= T_foc?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Open Problem 9 because §4.4 introduces exactly the C^2-valued cubic vectorial equation (3)vect, immediately recalls via Remark 2 that the scalar model is a special case, and then asks for the vectorial counterparts of the earlier scalar open problems. Your listed examples line up with several of the referenced scalar problems—especially Open Problems 4–8 and 10—but the official statement is slightly broader, since it points back to the full collection of scalar open problems from §§4.1–4.3 and 4.5. The refined version therefore keeps your intended emphasis while restoring the paper’s exact scope and assumptions.
